components.title: External funding and long commitments in 2026

components.text: Off balance sheet: Meta's 1 GW El Paso venture is 80% owned by BlackRock, and $12.5bn of its roughly $14bn cost is debt.

footnote: Source: Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle 10-Qs and SEC filings, Meta release, Nvidia CFO commentary (Jun to Sep 2026)
notes: The gap on the previous pages is now filled with outside money, in two ways. The first is plain debt and equity. Amazon has issued about $91.9bn of new notes this year, and the face value of its long-term debt went from $68.8bn at the end of 2025 to $133.0bn at the end of June. Alphabet issued about $51.8bn of debt in the first half and in June announced an $84.75bn equity package: common stock, mandatory convertible preferred, a $10bn private placement with Berkshire and a $40bn at-the-market facility, with $49.6bn of net proceeds in the quarter. Oracle used up its $20bn at-the-market facility in a single quarter. The second way stays off the balance sheet: long leases, joint ventures and guarantees. Meta signed about $68bn of new leases in July and set up a 1 GW campus in El Paso with BlackRock, which owns 80%, with $12.5bn of the roughly $14bn cost funded by debt. Nvidia guaranteed obligations for SB Energy's Ohio campus, which is leased to OpenAI for 20 years, up to $105bn.
